subject: Egress & DNS split-horizon model for private endpoint — minimal allowlist
messages:
From: Tara Singh <tara.singh@acmehealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: acme-security@acmehealth.com
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private endpoint deploy — egress constraints and DNS behavior

Hi Karthik / Laura / Priyom,

Thanks for taking this on. We're preparing the VPC/private-deploy for Redwood's private endpoint and need to lock down outbound behaviour before we sign off. Attached is a high-level spreadsheet with our security team's requirements (egress-requirements.xlsx). Key asks: 

- Minimal outbound allowlist: we want to limit all private endpoint egress to a small, auditable set of IPs and FQDNs.
- Split-horizon DNS: internal resolution for redwood.internal should point at the private endpoint; external (public) resolution must not leak private IPs. We need guidance on whether Redwood expects us to manage DNS or if the private control plane will provide records.
- All telemetry, metrics and crash reporting must exit via our customer proxy (proxy.acmehealth.local) or through a customer's NAT; traffic must never be allowed directly to public telemetry endpoints.
- TLS inspection is out — we cannot terminate TLS mid-flight.

Can you confirm what the minimal set of IPs/FQDNs Redwood needs to allow outbound for control-plane and model fetch? Also: does Redwood require DNS PTR lookups or outbound access to any cloud metadata services during startup?

We'd like to move quickly — is a 30 minute call possible today to go over specifics?

Thanks,
Tara Singh
Director, Infrastructure Security
Acme Health

Attachments: egress-requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42KB)
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Tara Singh <tara.singh@acmehealth.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private endpoint deploy — egress constraints and DNS behavior

Hi Tara — thanks for the clear list and the spreadsheet. Quick ack and an initial plan: 

1) Minimal allowlist: at a high level Redwood private runtime needs outbound to: 
   - Control-plane endpoints (management & metrics): control.redwood-inference.com (we can provide IP ranges and should be fine if you do FQDN allowlisting to those FQDNs + port 443).
   - Model store (only if you opt in to remote model pulls): model-cdn.redwood-inference.net. If you pre-bundle models or host them internally, this is optional.
   - Image/container registries (optional, only for on-prem installs where Redwood pulls sidecars).

We'll produce a concise list of FQDNs and stable IP prefixes for your firewall team — I'll attach a starter snippet for firewall rules (proposed-fw-snippets.txt).

2) DNS split-horizon: Redwood's private deployment supports two options:
   - Customer-managed split-horizon DNS (recommended): you author internal zones so redwood.internal resolves to private IPs. Redwood points at whatever internal A/AAAA you provide.
   - Redwood-managed private DNS: we can optionally publish internal records into your VPC via a delegated zone (requires VPC peering / private hosted zone setup). This adds operational overhead and needs an IAM operation.

3) Telemetry / egress via proxy: we can route telemetry to an endpoint you specify. Runtime supports configuring an HTTP(S) proxy and a list of endpoints that must be tunneled through it; we do not require TLS termination. We will not reach out to third-party telemetry services unless explicitly enabled.

Clarifications needed from your side:
- Will you allow FQDN-based egress rules (SSL inspection not required), or do you strictly require IP-based allowlists? IP-only rules are harder because some providers use large CDNs and ephemeral IPs.
- Confirm whether model updates will be pulled from Redwood model-cdn or you will host models internally.
- Please confirm whether the customer proxy requires mutual TLS / client certs for outbound.

I can do a short call at 13:00 PST today if that works for you.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Private Deployments, Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed-fw-snippets.txt (text, 3KB)
From: Tara Singh <tara.singh@acmehealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: acme-security@acmehealth.com, NOC Ops <noc.ops@edgeproxy.io>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 13:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private endpoint deploy — egress constraints and DNS behavior

Karthik — thanks, that helps. Quick answers inline:

- FQDN-based rules are acceptable for most egress controls; our firewall team prefers FQDN + application-layer allow rules for port 443. For a small set of critical infra (control plane) we will also add IP-based pins for extra assurance.
- We will host the primary models internally (so model-cdn access can be disabled). However, we will allow the model store for occasional updates during maintenance windows if we have explicit scheduling and IP pins.
- Customer proxy requires TLS client auth for outbound connections (we'll provide certs and a CA).

One additional constraint: internal DNS MUST NOT resolve public-facing control plane endpoints to private IPs (we will not accept split-horizon that causes outbound to exit via public internet). Basically: internal names -> private endpoints only; public names -> public IPs.

I've attached an updated network diagram (network-diagram-v2.png) that shows the proxy and NAT path we expect. NOC Ops is copied to confirm whether their edge proxy needs any specific headers or SNI passthrough.

Tara

Subject: Re: Private endpoint deploy — egress constraints and DNS behavior

Hi Tara — following up with a concise operational plan based on our call and the messages below. Please treat this as the agreed minimal allowlist and next steps; I'll open NETOPS-412 to track implementation and validation.

Summary of agreed minimal egress surface (customer-managed by firewall rules):
- control.redwood-inference.com (FQDN) port 443 — IP pins: 34.210.50.0/24, 52.23.11.0/24 (we will provide final list). Purpose: control-plane heartbeats, rollout commands, metrics push.
- proxy-only telemetry: all telemetry endpoints must be reachable only via proxy.acmehealth.local:443 with client cert mTLS. Runtime will not initiate direct connections to telemetry.redwood-inference.com unless explicitly enabled.
- model pulls: disabled by default. If enabled, restricted to scheduled windows and the same IP-pinning policy as control-plane above.
- container/image registries: disabled unless you opt in; if enabled we'll provide IP ranges to pin.

Firewall rule snippets (high-level, apply in order):
1) Allow outbound to proxy.acmehealth.local:443 (mTLS required).
2) Allow outbound to control.redwood-inference.com:443 (IPs pinned).
3) Deny outbound to public telemetry or CDN ranges except during maintenance windows.
4) Allow DNS (UDP/TCP 53) only to internal resolvers (no direct public DNS).

DNS guidance:
- Customer-managed split-horizon: create internal A records for redwood.private.example -> private endpoint IPs; public records must remain pointing at the public endpoint. Do not configure internal zones that resolve public control-plane FQDNs to private IPs.
- We will consume your internal resolver or a delegated zone if you prefer; delegation will require the usual IAM/route53 access.

Validation plan:
- Step 1: Apply firewall rules in a staging VPC and run smoke tests (control-plane handshake, model access disabled).
- Step 2: Run telemetry assertion that all telemetry egress flows through proxy (we will ship a small agent and a validation checklist).
- Step 3: Schedule a 1-hour joint test window to verify DNS split-horizon behaviour and iptables checks.

Next steps for Acme ops:
- Share client cert bundle for proxy and the CA fingerprint.
- Confirm whether your firewall supports FQDN deny/allow with SNI inspection disabled.
- Provide a staging VPC and CI creds for our validation runs (we will only use them for the smoke tests and will log access).

I'll update NETOPS-412 and attach the final pinned IP list and the txt firewall snippets. Reach out if you'd prefer a quick hangout to walk through the rules.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Sr. Infra Engineer, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
